content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I created a program a few years ago with assistance from [user_name], using an analog 4-20 mA sensor and a 500 ohm resistor in series. I connected this setup to an input of the [product_name] for 0-10 volts measurement. The system worked well until recently when, instead of displaying 0 bar, it shows -0.04 bar at zero and doesn't register correctly at the starting point, although readings above zero function normally. How can I resolve this through programming? Alternatively, could the change in resistance (measured at 498 ohms instead of 500) be affecting the results?
There can be various causes for the reading dropping to -0.04 bar instead of starting at zero. In your program, you could set it so that any value below 0 bar is fixed at 0 bar for display purposes.
How can I implement that, please?
I've attached an example for reference.
Can I use the same method for a 4-20 mA sensor here with [user_name]?
Yes, the example applies to a 4-20 mA sensor setup.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing a slight negative offset in pressure readings from a 4-20 mA analog sensor connected to a [product_name], resulting in values not starting exactly at zero. The conversation centers around resolving this either through programming logic—such as clamping readings below zero to zero—or by checking and adjusting hardware components like resistors. There is an emphasis on achieving an accurate zero-point calibration and understanding both software and hardware factors affecting sensor output.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect precise sensor readings that start from zero bar, without any negative offset. They are looking for straightforward solutions, whether through programming adjustments or hardware calibration, to correct and maintain accurate sensor outputs.
